edges.source_hint: UDC 1 (Philosophy); LCC B (Philosophy — General)
edges.rationale: Philosophy is the canonical primary discipline of the humanities; UDC class 1 and LCC class B are both reserved for it at the top division level.
edges.uncertainty: No meaningful uncertainty — this is the anchor edge named in the batch manifest.

edges.source_hint: UDC 111 (Metaphysics); LCC BD95–BD131 (Metaphysics)
edges.rationale: Metaphysics is one of the five traditional divisions of philosophy recognised in every classification scheme; UDC 111 and LCC BD give it a dedicated numbered division.
edges.uncertainty: Classification sources agree; no contested placement known.

edges.source_hint: UDC 111.1 (Ontology); LCC BD300–BD450 (Ontology — Being, Existence, Essence)
edges.rationale: Ontology is a core philosophical sub-area studying being and existence; UDC 111.1 and LCC BD300-450 classify it within philosophy. Per §12 precedent, ontology is a peer of metaphysics at the same level under field:philosophy.
edges.uncertainty: Some classify ontology as a subdivision of metaphysics rather than a peer branch; the skeleton precedent (2026-06-10) treats them as peers, which is reflected here.

edges.source_hint: UDC 165 (Theory of knowledge / Epistemology); LCC BD143–BD237 (Epistemology)
edges.rationale: Epistemology is one of the five canonical divisions of philosophy; UDC 165 and LCC BD143-237 give it a dedicated numbered slot within the philosophy classification.
edges.uncertainty: No contested placement; universally classified under philosophy.

edges.source_hint: UDC 17 (Ethics / Moral philosophy); LCC BJ (Ethics)
edges.rationale: Ethics is one of the five canonical branches of philosophy; UDC 17 and LCC BJ are dedicated top-level philosophy divisions for moral philosophy.
edges.uncertainty: No contested placement.

edges.source_hint: UDC 16 (Logic); LCC BC (Logic) under philosophy class B; PhilPapers Logic taxonomy
edges.rationale: Logic is housed in domain:humanities per the /data node assignment; UDC 16 and LCC BC place logic within the philosophy class cluster; PhilPapers treats logic as a primary philosophy area. The node represents philosophical/informal logic, not mathematical logic (which has its own formal-sciences node).
edges.uncertainty: Logic is strongly cross-listed with formal sciences (mathematical logic, subfield:mathematical-logic); the humanities placement reflects the philosophical-logic reading of the node, but QC should confirm that subfield:logic and subfield:mathematical-logic cover distinct communities and do not overlap.

edges.source_hint: UDC 18 (Aesthetics / Philosophy of art); LCC BH (Aesthetics)
edges.rationale: Aesthetics is one of the five canonical divisions of philosophy; UDC 18 and LCC BH are dedicated top-level philosophy divisions.
edges.uncertainty: No contested placement.

edges.source_hint: UDC 17 (Ethics / Axiology broadly); LCC BJ (Ethics / Value theory); PhilPapers Value Theory taxonomy
edges.rationale: Axiology is the philosophical study of value; LCC BJ covers value theory alongside ethics, and PhilPapers treats it as a primary philosophy division. Parent is field:philosophy because axiology has no closer intermediate parent in the flat two-level skeleton.
edges.uncertainty: Axiology overlaps substantially with ethics; some classification schemes do not distinguish axiology from ethics at this level, which could make the node partially redundant with subfield:ethics.

edges.source_hint: UDC 159.9:1 (Philosophy of psychology / Philosophy of mind); LCC BD418–BD418.5 (Mind-body problem); PhilPapers Philosophy of Mind taxonomy
edges.rationale: Philosophy of mind is a primary area of contemporary philosophy with dedicated LCC entries; PhilPapers lists it as one of its top-level categories.
edges.uncertainty: Deep overlap with cognitive sciences; some classify philosophy of mind partly under cognitive-sciences domain.

edges.source_hint: UDC 1:80 (Philosophy of language); LCC P105–P107 (Language and languages — Philosophy); PhilPapers Philosophy of Language taxonomy
edges.rationale: Philosophy of language is a primary branch of analytic philosophy; PhilPapers lists it as a top-level area; LCC P-class gives it dedicated entries within linguistics-adjacent classification.
edges.uncertainty: LCC files philosophy of language partly under class P (Language) rather than class B (Philosophy), which is a mild cross-classification. The institutional home (philosophy departments) makes field:philosophy the correct parent.

edges.source_hint: UDC 001.1 (Philosophy of science); LCC Q175 (Science — Philosophy); PhilPapers Philosophy of Science taxonomy
edges.rationale: Philosophy of science is a core branch of philosophy housed in philosophy departments worldwide; PhilPapers treats it as a top-level area.
edges.uncertainty: LCC files philosophy of science under Q (Science) rather than B (Philosophy), reflecting a mild dual-classification; institutional home is philosophy departments.

edges.source_hint: UDC 51:1 (Philosophy of mathematics); LCC QA8–QA8.9 (Mathematics — Philosophy); PhilPapers Philosophy of Mathematics taxonomy
edges.rationale: Philosophy of mathematics is a major branch of analytic philosophy; PhilPapers lists it as a top-level area; it is housed in philosophy departments, not mathematics departments.
edges.uncertainty: Dual classification in both LCC Q (Mathematics) and LCC B (Philosophy); the institutional primary home is philosophy departments, which determines field:philosophy as parent.

edges.source_hint: UDC 1:2 (Philosophy of religion); LCC BL51 (Religion — Philosophy); PhilPapers Philosophy of Religion taxonomy
edges.rationale: Philosophy of religion is a standard division in philosophy departments; LCC BL51 and UDC 1:2 classify it within the philosophy-adjacent cluster.
edges.uncertainty: May be jointly housed in religious studies departments; LCC places it under BL (Religion), but it is standardly taught in philosophy departments.

edges.source_hint: UDC 34:1 (Philosophy of law / Jurisprudence — Philosophy); LCC K237 (Jurisprudence — Philosophy); PhilPapers Philosophy of Law taxonomy
edges.rationale: Philosophy of law (jurisprudence) is a recognised sub-area of philosophy with dedicated PhilPapers taxonomy; taught in both law and philosophy departments.
edges.uncertainty: Often housed in law schools rather than philosophy departments; LCC files it under K (Law). The philosophical analysis of law is the philosophy-department portion, but the placement boundary is porous.

edges.source_hint: UDC 32:1 (Political philosophy); LCC JC (Political theory / The state); PhilPapers Social and Political Philosophy taxonomy
edges.rationale: Political philosophy is a primary branch of philosophy with dedicated LCC JC entries; taught in both philosophy and political science departments; PhilPapers gives it major taxonomy coverage.
edges.uncertainty: Political science departments also claim political theory; the philosophy-side institutional presence justifies field:philosophy as parent, but the cross-listing is real.

edges.source_hint: UDC 316:1 (Sociology — Philosophy / Social philosophy); LCC HM (Sociology — General, includes social philosophy); PhilPapers Social Philosophy taxonomy
edges.rationale: Social philosophy is a recognised branch of philosophy examining social institutions, justice, and human nature; taught in philosophy departments; PhilPapers covers it.
edges.uncertainty: LCC files social philosophy partly under HM (Sociology); boundary with political philosophy and sociology is blurry.

edges.source_hint: UDC 159.9:1 (Philosophy of psychology / action theory); LCC B105.A35 (Action — Philosophical aspects); PhilPapers Action Theory taxonomy
edges.rationale: Philosophy of action is a core area of analytic philosophy, studying intentionality, agency, and reasons for action; PhilPapers lists action theory as a top-level area.
edges.uncertainty: Closely overlaps with philosophy of mind; no separate UDC or LCC division exists — the source hint points to the nearest proxy entries.

edges.source_hint: UDC 165.6 (Sensationalism / Theory of perception); LCC B828.45 (Phenomenology of perception); PhilPapers Philosophy of Perception taxonomy
edges.rationale: Philosophy of perception is a recognised sub-area of analytic philosophy and phenomenology; PhilPapers covers it as a substantial taxonomy node.
edges.uncertainty: Overlaps with both philosophy-of-mind and phenomenology; independent UDC/LCC classifications are sparse — source hints are approximate proxy entries.

edges.source_hint: UDC 1:62 (Philosophy of technology); LCC T14 (Technology — Philosophy); PhilPapers Philosophy of Technology taxonomy
edges.rationale: Philosophy of technology is a recognised sub-area of philosophy with LCC T14 classification and PhilPapers coverage; studied in both philosophy and science-and-technology-studies departments.
edges.uncertainty: Sits at the boundary between philosophy, STS, and engineering ethics; the philosophy-department home justifies field:philosophy as parent.

edges.source_hint: UDC 57:1 (Philosophy of biology); LCC QH331 (Biology — Philosophy); PhilPapers Philosophy of Biology taxonomy
edges.rationale: Philosophy of biology is a major branch of philosophy of science with dedicated LCC QH331 classification; standard area in philosophy of science programs.
edges.uncertainty: LCC files it under QH (Natural History/Biology), not under B (Philosophy). Institutional home is philosophy departments.

edges.source_hint: UDC 53:1 (Philosophy of physics); LCC QC6 (Physics — Philosophy); PhilPapers Philosophy of Physical Science taxonomy
edges.rationale: Philosophy of physics is a major branch of philosophy of science; LCC QC6 and PhilPapers give it dedicated coverage; standard sub-area in philosophy departments.
edges.uncertainty: LCC files it under QC (Physics), not under B (Philosophy). Institutional home is philosophy departments.

edges.source_hint: UDC 3:1 (Philosophy of social sciences); LCC H61 (Social sciences — Methodology / Philosophy); PhilPapers Philosophy of Social Science taxonomy
edges.rationale: Philosophy of social science examines the methodology and foundations of the social sciences; PhilPapers and LCC H61 give it dedicated entries; taught in philosophy departments.
edges.uncertainty: Sometimes housed in social science methodology departments rather than philosophy; LCC places it under H (Social sciences).

edges.source_hint: UDC 17:61 (Ethics of medicine / Bioethics); LCC QH332 (Bioethics); PhilPapers Applied Ethics > Bioethics taxonomy
edges.rationale: Bioethics is a primary applied ethics sub-area housed in philosophy departments and medical schools; PhilPapers covers it as a major ethics sub-area.
edges.uncertainty: Often taught in medical schools and nursing programs, not solely in philosophy departments; cross-listed with medicine-and-health domain.

edges.source_hint: UDC 17:504 (Environmental ethics); LCC GE42 (Environmental ethics); PhilPapers Applied Ethics > Environmental Ethics taxonomy
edges.rationale: Environmental ethics is a primary sub-area of applied ethics, housed in philosophy departments; PhilPapers covers it as a major ethics sub-area.
edges.uncertainty: LCC GE42 places it under Environmental Sciences rather than Philosophy; the philosophical subdiscipline is in philosophy departments.

edges.source_hint: UDC 17:33 (Ethics and economics / Business ethics); LCC HF5387 (Business ethics); PhilPapers Applied Ethics > Business Ethics taxonomy
edges.rationale: Business ethics is a primary sub-area of applied ethics; PhilPapers covers it; the philosophical analysis of business practices is taught in philosophy and business school ethics courses.
edges.uncertainty: Primarily housed in business schools (LCC HF) rather than philosophy departments; the philosophy-department presence is real but secondary in many institutions.

edges.source_hint: UDC 17 (Ethics — metaethical questions); LCC BJ1012 (Ethics — General and theoretical); PhilPapers Metaethics taxonomy
edges.rationale: Metaethics is a major sub-area of philosophy studying the nature of moral facts, moral language, and moral epistemology; PhilPapers lists it as one of the primary ethics sub-areas.
edges.uncertainty: No disputed placement; universally classified under ethics within philosophy.

edges.source_hint: UDC 17 (Ethics — normative theory); LCC BJ1012–BJ1188 (Normative ethics); PhilPapers Normative Ethics taxonomy
edges.rationale: Normative ethics is a primary sub-area of moral philosophy studying ethical theories (consequentialism, deontology, virtue ethics); PhilPapers lists it as a top-level ethics division.
edges.uncertainty: No disputed placement.

edges.source_hint: UDC 165.6/.8 (Analytical philosophy); LCC B808–B808.5 (Analytic philosophy); PhilPapers Analytic Philosophy taxonomy
edges.rationale: Analytic philosophy is a major tradition-axis subfield within philosophy; LCC B808 and PhilPapers give it a dedicated place.
edges.uncertainty: As a tradition/methodology axis rather than a topical division, some classification schemes do not give it a distinct slot; the §12 precedent retains tradition/methodology axes as subfields.

edges.source_hint: UDC 1(4) (European / Continental philosophy); LCC B72 (Philosophy — Continental European); PhilPapers Continental Philosophy taxonomy
edges.rationale: Continental philosophy is a major tradition-axis subfield within philosophy; LCC B72 and PhilPapers give it dedicated coverage.
edges.uncertainty: As a tradition axis, placement within any single classification scheme is approximate; some classification systems do not distinguish Continental from Analytic philosophy at the division level.

edges.source_hint: UDC 165.62 (Phenomenology); LCC B829 (Phenomenology); PhilPapers Phenomenology taxonomy
edges.rationale: Phenomenology is a major methodological sub-area of philosophy with dedicated LCC B829 classification; founded by Husserl and central to Continental philosophy.
edges.uncertainty: Also a methodology used within cognitive science and psychology; the philosophical tradition is primary.

edges.source_hint: UDC 165.61 (Existentialism); LCC B819 (Existentialism); PhilPapers Existentialism taxonomy
edges.rationale: Existentialism is a major philosophical movement/methodology sub-area with dedicated LCC B819 classification; studied as a distinct tradition in all philosophy curricula.
edges.uncertainty: Academic status is 'established' but the existentialism research programme in its classic form is largely historical; contemporary descendants (existential phenomenology) are active.

edges.source_hint: UDC 165.6 (Pragmatism); LCC B832 (Pragmatism); PhilPapers Pragmatism taxonomy
edges.rationale: Pragmatism is a major American philosophical tradition with dedicated LCC B832 classification; active research program through neo-pragmatism.
edges.uncertainty: As a tradition/methodology axis, some classification schemes do not give it a distinct sub-area slot.

edges.source_hint: UDC 14 (Philosophical systems and schools — Ancient); LCC B108–B708 (Ancient philosophy); PhilPapers Ancient Greek and Roman Philosophy taxonomy
edges.rationale: Ancient philosophy is a major historical sub-area of philosophy with extensive LCC coverage (B108-708); standard required area in all philosophy programs.
edges.uncertainty: No disputed placement.

edges.source_hint: UDC 14 (Philosophical systems — Medieval); LCC B720–B765 (Medieval philosophy); PhilPapers Medieval and Renaissance Philosophy taxonomy
edges.rationale: Medieval philosophy is a major historical sub-area with dedicated LCC coverage; present as a named research specialization in every major philosophy department.
edges.uncertainty: No disputed placement.

edges.source_hint: UDC 14 (Philosophical systems — Renaissance); LCC B770–B779 (Renaissance philosophy); PhilPapers Medieval and Renaissance Philosophy taxonomy
edges.rationale: Renaissance philosophy is a recognised historical sub-area; LCC B770-779 gives it dedicated coverage; standard specialisation in history of philosophy.
edges.uncertainty: Sometimes subsumed under 'early modern philosophy' rather than listed as a separate period; boundary with medieval and modern philosophy is fuzzy.

edges.source_hint: UDC 1(510) (Chinese philosophy); LCC B125–B128 (Philosophy — China); PhilPapers Chinese Philosophy taxonomy
edges.rationale: Chinese philosophy is a major non-Western philosophical tradition; LCC B125-128 and PhilPapers give it dedicated coverage.
edges.uncertainty: No disputed placement within philosophy.

edges.source_hint: UDC 1(540) (Indian philosophy); LCC B130–B133 (Philosophy — India); PhilPapers Indian Philosophy taxonomy
edges.rationale: Indian philosophy is a major non-Western philosophical tradition; LCC B130-133 and PhilPapers give it dedicated coverage.
edges.uncertainty: No disputed placement.

edges.source_hint: UDC 1(=727) (Buddhist philosophy); LCC BQ (Buddhism — general, includes philosophical texts); PhilPapers Buddhist Philosophy taxonomy
edges.rationale: Buddhist philosophy is a recognised philosophical tradition; PhilPapers gives it dedicated taxonomy; many philosophy departments have Buddhist philosophy specialists.
edges.uncertainty: LCC files Buddhist philosophy under BQ (Religion / Buddhism) rather than B (Philosophy); the philosophical tradition is distinct from the religious practice but shares the same classification.

edges.source_hint: UDC 1(=411.21) (Islamic philosophy); LCC B741–B753 (Islamic philosophy); PhilPapers Islamic Philosophy taxonomy
edges.rationale: Islamic philosophy is a major tradition within the history of philosophy; LCC B741-753 gives it dedicated coverage.
edges.uncertainty: No disputed placement.

edges.source_hint: UDC 1(=411.16) (Jewish philosophy); LCC B154–B159 (Jewish philosophy); PhilPapers Jewish Philosophy taxonomy
edges.rationale: Jewish philosophy is a recognised tradition in the history of philosophy; LCC B154-159 gives it dedicated coverage.
edges.uncertainty: No disputed placement.

edges.source_hint: UDC 1(6) (African philosophy); LCC B5300–B5305 (Philosophy — Africa); PhilPapers African Philosophy taxonomy
edges.rationale: African philosophy is a growing area in the philosophy curriculum; LCC B5300-5305 and PhilPapers give it dedicated coverage.
edges.uncertainty: Institutional department-level presence is thinner than Western traditions; the academic recognition is established via journals (Journal of African Philosophy, African Studies) and PhilPapers.

edges.source_hint: UDC 1(520) (Japanese philosophy); LCC B5240–B5244 (Philosophy — Japan); PhilPapers Japanese Philosophy taxonomy
edges.rationale: Japanese philosophy is a recognised tradition including the Kyoto School; LCC B5240-5244 gives it coverage; PhilPapers lists it.
edges.uncertainty: Department-level presence outside Japan is limited; academic recognition is established primarily through specialist journals and PhilPapers.

edges.source_hint: UDC 1(519) (Korean philosophy); LCC B5253–B5256 (Philosophy — Korea); PhilPapers East Asian Philosophy taxonomy
edges.rationale: Korean philosophy is a recognised tradition within comparative and East Asian philosophy; LCC B5253-5256 gives it dedicated coverage.
edges.uncertainty: Department-level presence outside Korea is limited; LCC classification range is narrow. PhilPapers covers it within East Asian philosophy.

edges.source_hint: UDC 1(7/8) (Philosophy of the Americas); LCC B1000–B1099 (Philosophy — Latin America); PhilPapers Latin American Philosophy taxonomy
edges.rationale: Latin American philosophy is a recognised tradition; LCC B1000-1099 gives it dedicated coverage; PhilPapers lists it as a major area.
edges.uncertainty: Institutional home is primarily in Latin American universities; global recognition is growing but department-level presence in North American/European institutions is still developing.

edges.source_hint: UDC 1(100) (Comparative philosophy broadly); LCC B799 (Comparative philosophy); PhilPapers Comparative Philosophy taxonomy
edges.rationale: Comparative philosophy is a recognised methodology/area comparing traditions across cultures; PhilPapers covers it and it has dedicated journals (Philosophy East and West).
edges.uncertainty: As a methodological orientation rather than a tradition with its own content, it overlaps with all non-Western philosophy sub-areas; the classification boundary is porous.

edges.source_hint: UDC 1:93 (Philosophy of history); LCC D16 (History — Philosophy); PhilPapers Philosophy of History taxonomy
edges.rationale: Philosophy of history is a recognised sub-area of philosophy studying the nature and methodology of historical inquiry; PhilPapers covers it.
edges.uncertainty: LCC files it under D (World History) rather than B (Philosophy); institutional home is philosophy departments.

edges.source_hint: UDC 1:33 (Philosophy of economics); LCC HB72 (Economics — Philosophy); PhilPapers Philosophy of Economics taxonomy
edges.rationale: Philosophy of economics is a recognised sub-area of philosophy of social science; PhilPapers covers it as a major taxonomy node.
edges.uncertainty: LCC files it under HB (Economics) rather than B (Philosophy); frequently cross-listed between philosophy and economics departments.

edges.source_hint: UDC 1:305 (Feminist philosophy); LCC B105.F45 (Feminism — Philosophical aspects); PhilPapers Feminist Philosophy taxonomy
edges.rationale: Feminist philosophy is a recognised sub-area of philosophy studying gender, power, and epistemology from feminist perspectives; PhilPapers lists it as a top-level area.
edges.uncertainty: Sometimes cross-listed with gender studies / women's studies departments rather than pure philosophy.

edges.source_hint: UDC 37.01 (Philosophy of education); LCC LB14.7 (Education — Philosophy); PhilPapers Philosophy of Education taxonomy
edges.rationale: Philosophy of education is a recognised sub-area examining educational aims, practice, and policy from a philosophical perspective; PhilPapers covers it.
edges.uncertainty: Primarily housed in schools of education rather than philosophy departments; LCC files it under L (Education).

edges.source_hint: UDC 165.43 (Hermeneutics); LCC BD241 (Hermeneutics); PhilPapers Hermeneutics taxonomy
edges.rationale: Hermeneutics is a major methodology/sub-area of Continental philosophy with dedicated LCC BD241 classification.
edges.uncertainty: Also used as a method in theology, literary theory, and law; the philosophical tradition is primary.

edges.source_hint: UDC 101 (Metaphilosophy / Nature of philosophy); LCC B53 (Philosophy — General works, nature of philosophy); PhilPapers Metaphilosophy taxonomy
edges.rationale: Metaphilosophy is a recognised self-reflective sub-area of philosophy studying the nature and method of philosophy itself; PhilPapers covers it.
edges.uncertainty: LCC B53 is a broad classification; the dedicated metaphilosophy area may be harder to ground at a finer LCC level.

edges.source_hint: UDC 1:5 (Natural philosophy); LCC Q (Science — General, including natural philosophy historically); PhilPapers Natural Philosophy / History of Science taxonomy
edges.rationale: Natural philosophy is a historical sub-area of philosophy (pre-modern precursor to natural science); academic_status is 'historical'; it remains a research area in history and philosophy of science.
edges.uncertainty: As a historical sub-area, its living academic community is primarily within history and philosophy of science; the LCC classification is approximate.

edges.source_hint: UDC 141.4 (Scholasticism); LCC B720–B745 (Medieval philosophy, including Scholasticism); PhilPapers Medieval Philosophy taxonomy
edges.rationale: Scholasticism is a major historical philosophical methodology of the medieval period; LCC B720-745 covers medieval and scholastic philosophy; academic_status is 'historical'.
edges.uncertainty: As a historical tradition, its primary contemporary study is in history of philosophy; neo-scholasticism is a living but minor contemporary movement.

edges.source_hint: UDC 1:616.89 (Philosophy of psychiatry); LCC RC437.5 (Psychiatry — Philosophy); PhilPapers Philosophy of Psychiatry taxonomy
edges.rationale: Philosophy of psychiatry is an emerging sub-area of philosophy of medicine and philosophy of science; PhilPapers covers it; the International Association for Philosophy and Psychiatry (IAPP) provides institutional grounding.
edges.uncertainty: LCC files it under RC (Medicine — Psychiatry) rather than B (Philosophy); primarily housed in medical and psychiatric institutions.

edges.source_hint: UDC 1:007 (Philosophy of information); LCC Q350–Q360 (Information theory — Philosophy); PhilPapers Philosophy of Information taxonomy
edges.rationale: Philosophy of information is an emerging sub-area studying the nature of information, computation, and knowledge; associated with Luciano Floridi's work; PhilPapers covers it.
edges.uncertainty: Overlaps substantially with philosophy-of-technology and philosophy-of-mind; emerging area with thin LCC classification coverage.

edges.source_hint: UDC 17:004 (Ethics and computing / AI ethics); LCC Q335 (AI — Moral and ethical aspects); PhilPapers Applied Ethics > Ethics of Artificial Intelligence taxonomy
edges.rationale: Ethics of AI is an emerging applied ethics area; PhilPapers covers it; growing institutional presence in philosophy and computer science departments.
edges.uncertainty: Cross-listed between philosophy and computer science; institutional home is contested and rapidly evolving.

edges.source_hint: UDC 165.8 (Empirical approaches to philosophy); LCC B53 (Philosophy — Methodology); PhilPapers Experimental Philosophy taxonomy
edges.rationale: Experimental philosophy is an emerging methodology within analytic philosophy using empirical methods; PhilPapers covers it with dedicated taxonomy.
edges.uncertainty: As a methodology rather than a topical area, its status as a distinct subfield is debated within philosophy; the thin UDC/LCC classification reflects this.

edges.source_hint: UDC 519.8:1 (Decision theory — philosophical aspects); LCC BD (Philosophy of action / Practical reason); PhilPapers Decision Theory taxonomy
edges.rationale: decision-theory is classified under domain:humanities in /data; the philosophical study of rational choice is a primary area in action theory and formal epistemology; PhilPapers covers it.
edges.uncertainty: Decision theory is strongly cross-listed with formal sciences (economics, mathematics, operations-research); the philosophy-side placement reflects the normative/epistemological interpretation of the /data node, but QC should confirm this edge does not conflict with any planned formal-sciences-side placement.

edges.source_hint: UDC 133 (Occultism / Esotericism); LCC BF1428–BF1999 (Occult sciences); PhilPapers — no dedicated primary taxonomy
edges.rationale: Esotericism and theosophy is classified under domain:humanities in /data with academic_status 'non_academic'; it is studied academically as a religious/philosophical phenomenon by scholars in the European Society for the Study of Western Esotericism.
edges.uncertainty: This node has academic_status 'non_academic'; parent assignment to field:philosophy reflects the closest classification home, but the community is primarily in religious studies departments (LCC BF) rather than philosophy departments.

edges.source_hint: UDC 14 (Philosophical systems — Modern); LCC B790–B849 (Modern philosophy); PhilPapers Modern Philosophy taxonomy
edges.rationale: Modern philosophy (17th–19th century) is a major historical sub-area of philosophy with dedicated LCC B790-849 coverage.
edges.uncertainty: Boundary with renaissance-philosophy (preceding) and contemporary analytic/continental (following) is fuzzy; some schemes subsume it differently.

edges.source_hint: UDC 165.74 (Critical theory / Frankfurt School); LCC B809.3 (Critical theory); PhilPapers Critical Theory taxonomy
edges.rationale: Critical theory (Frankfurt School tradition) is a recognised sub-area of Continental philosophy with dedicated LCC B809.3 classification.
edges.uncertainty: Cross-listed with social theory and sociology departments; the term 'critical theory' is also used more broadly in literary and cultural studies.

edges.source_hint: UDC 1:323.1 (Philosophy and race); LCC B105.R33 (Race — Philosophical aspects); PhilPapers Philosophy of Race taxonomy
edges.rationale: Philosophy of race is an emerging area studying the metaphysics, epistemology, and ethics of race; PhilPapers covers it as a major area in social/political philosophy.
edges.uncertainty: LCC coverage is sparse; primarily classified under B105 (miscellaneous topics); institutional home is philosophy departments but also ethnic studies.

edges.source_hint: UDC 159.9:1 (Philosophy of psychology/cognitive science); LCC BF311 (Cognitive science — Philosophy); PhilPapers Philosophy of Cognitive Science taxonomy
edges.rationale: Philosophy of cognitive science is a recognised sub-area of philosophy of mind and science; PhilPapers covers it as a primary area.
edges.uncertainty: Strongly overlaps with philosophy-of-mind; the cognitive-science domain also claims it. Dual classification is real.

edges.source_hint: UDC 007 (Communication and control theory / Systems science); LCC Q295 (System theory); International Society for the Systems Sciences (ISSS)
edges.rationale: Systems science is classified as a branch of the formal sciences alongside mathematics and statistics; UDC 007 and LCC Q295 place it within the formal/general sciences cluster; named in the batch manifest as anchor.
edges.uncertainty: Institutional home is often within engineering and management faculties rather than a standalone formal-sciences department; UDC 007 is a broad class covering control theory, cybernetics, and systems science together.

edges.source_hint: UDC 510.6 (Mathematical logic); LCC QA9 (Logic — Mathematics); MSC 2020 section 03
edges.rationale: Mathematical logic is classified within mathematics by MSC 2020 (section 03), LCC QA9, and UDC 510.6; the /data node was demoted from field to subfield per QC ruling 2026-06-10, confirming its position within field:mathematics.
edges.uncertainty: MSC 03 is a peer top-level section alongside algebra, geometry, etc., which could argue for field:mathematics as parent; the QC demotion ruling settled this: mathematical-logic is a subfield within mathematics.

edges.source_hint: UDC 512 (Algebra); LCC QA150–QA272 (Algebra); MSC 2020 sections 08, 12, 13, 16, 17, 20
edges.rationale: Algebra is one of the four canonical branches of mathematics; UDC 512, LCC QA150-272, and MSC sections 08-20 place it squarely within mathematics.
edges.uncertainty: No contested placement.

edges.source_hint: UDC 511 (Number theory); LCC QA241–QA247 (Number theory); MSC 2020 section 11
edges.rationale: Number theory is one of the oldest and most active branches of mathematics; UDC 511, LCC QA241-247, and MSC 11 unambiguously place it within mathematics.
edges.uncertainty: No contested placement.

edges.source_hint: UDC 514 (Geometry); LCC QA440–QA699 (Geometry); MSC 2020 sections 51, 52, 53
edges.rationale: Geometry is one of the four canonical branches of mathematics; UDC 514, LCC QA440-699, and MSC 51-53 place it within mathematics.
edges.uncertainty: No contested placement.

edges.source_hint: UDC 514.7 (Differential geometry); LCC QA641–QA670 (Differential geometry); MSC 2020 section 53
edges.rationale: Differential geometry is a major sub-area of mathematics; UDC 514.7, LCC QA641-670, and MSC 53 place it within mathematics.
edges.uncertainty: No contested placement within mathematics; however, overlap with mathematical physics and topology is substantial.

edges.source_hint: UDC 512.7 (Algebraic geometry); LCC QA564–QA581 (Algebraic geometry); MSC 2020 section 14
edges.rationale: Algebraic geometry is a major sub-area of mathematics; UDC 512.7, LCC QA564-581, and MSC 14 place it within mathematics.
edges.uncertainty: Sits at the border between algebra and geometry; both parent assignments (under algebra or under geometry) are plausible within mathematics.

edges.source_hint: UDC 515.1 (Topology); LCC QA611–QA614 (Topology); MSC 2020 sections 54, 55, 57
edges.rationale: Topology is a major branch of mathematics; UDC 515.1, LCC QA611-614, and MSC 54/55/57 place it within mathematics.
edges.uncertainty: No contested placement.

edges.source_hint: UDC 515.14 (Algebraic topology); LCC QA612 (Algebraic topology); MSC 2020 section 55
edges.rationale: Algebraic topology is classified within mathematics under UDC 515.14, LCC QA612, and MSC 55.
edges.uncertainty: Some would file algebraic-topology under topology rather than directly under field:mathematics as peer; per §12 flat skeleton, it is proposed here at the same level as topology.

edges.source_hint: UDC 517 (Mathematical analysis); LCC QA299–QA433 (Analysis); MSC 2020 sections 26, 28, 30, 40, 41, 42, 46
edges.rationale: Mathematical analysis is one of the four canonical branches of mathematics; UDC 517, LCC QA299-433, and MSC sections 26-46 place it within mathematics.

edges.rationale: Information theory is classified within mathematics by MSC 94 and partially by LCC Q360-380; its mathematical foundations (entropy, channel capacity) originated in applied mathematics.
edges.uncertainty: Strongly cross-listed with computer science (coding theory, communications) and electrical engineering; LCC Q360 is close to the science/engineering boundary. Flagged ambiguous per generation order mandate.

edges.source_hint: UDC 336:519 (Financial mathematics); LCC HG106 (Mathematical methods in finance); MSC 2020 section 91G

edges.rationale: MSC 93 and LCC QA402.3 classify control theory within mathematics/applied mathematics; it has strong mathematical content.

edges.rationale: Mathematical statistics is the theoretical core of field:statistics; LCC QA276 and MSC 62 place it within statistics.
edges.uncertainty: Very close to the parent field:statistics itself — mathematical statistics could be viewed as 'statistics done rigorously' rather than a distinct sub-area. Alternative parent could be field:mathematics via the mathematical analysis/probability theory lineage.

edges.source_hint: UDC 519.2 (Applied statistics broadly); LCC QA276–QA280 (Applied statistics); MSC 2020 section 62P
edges.rationale: Applied statistics is the application-facing core of field:statistics; LCC QA276-280 and MSC 62P place it within statistics.

edges.source_hint: UDC 007 (Cybernetics / Communication and control); American Society for Cybernetics; ISSS (International Society for the Systems Sciences); Kybernetes journal
edges.rationale: Cybernetics is the historical root of systems science; UDC 007 covers both cybernetics and systems science as a cluster; the American Society for Cybernetics and ISSS provide the institutional grounding for this placement.
edges.uncertainty: Cybernetics as a unified programme has largely dissolved; it is now more of a historical antecedent to control-theory, systems science, and computer science than a living sub-area of systems-science. Alternative parent could be field:mathematics via control-theory lineage. The /data node is already flagged ambiguous.

notes: All UDC and LCC classification hints are unverified pointers supplied for QC live-verification — they are NOT citations. QC must verify each hint before promotion.

The 14 existing part_of edges in /data are not duplicated: field:mathematics->domain:formal-sciences, field:statistics->domain:formal-sciences, subfield:linear-algebra->field:mathematics, subfield:probability-theory->field:mathematics, subfield:calculus->field:mathematics, subfield:optimization->field:mathematics are all present and excluded from this proposal.

Philosophy anchor: field:philosophy->domain:humanities is proposed as the first edge in this batch. All 62 philosophy subfields in /data (domain=humanities) are proposed with field:philosophy as parent per UDC class 1 / LCC class B coverage.
Formal sciences anchor: field:systems-science->domain:formal-sciences is proposed. field:mathematics and field:statistics already have anchors in /data.

Mathematical-logic pillars (set-theory, model-theory, proof-theory, computability-theory): proposed as part_of subfield:mathematical-logic per MSC 03 sub-section structure. Edge topology is deeper than two hops; §12 explicitly permits this. All four flagged ambiguous=true per the generation order mandate.

Statistics cluster (bayesian-statistics, time-series-analysis, computational-statistics, mathematical-statistics, applied-statistics): proposed as part_of field:statistics. bayesian-statistics, time-series-analysis, computational-statistics, and mathematical-statistics are flagged ambiguous=true per the generation order's statistics-cluster mandate. applied-statistics is not flagged ambiguous because its placement under field:statistics is unambiguous in LCC/MSC.

Applied/boundary areas (mathematical-physics, applied-mathematics, operations-research, game-theory, information-theory, financial-mathematics, mathematics-education, history-of-mathematics, control-theory, mathematical-biology): all proposed as part_of field:mathematics per primary MSC/LCC classification, all flagged ambiguous=true per the generation order mandate.
Cybernetics: proposed as part_of field:systems-science per UDC 007 and ISSS; flagged ambiguous=true.

Cross-listing policy: where a node arguably belongs under two parents (e.g. logic -> philosophy AND formal-sciences; decision-theory -> philosophy AND social-sciences/formal-sciences), only the primary parent per the /data domain assignment is proposed. The alternative parent is recorded in the uncertainty field. Multiple part_of edges per node are out of scope (parked policy).

Concept nodes (concept:vector-space, concept:random-variable, concept:probability-distribution) and method nodes (method:bayesian-inference, method:gradient-descent) are out of scope: they are not type=field or type=subfield.
field:computer-science, field:machine-learning, field:physics are out of scope (not domain=humanities or domain=formal_sciences).
